stem.text: Evaluate the improper integral \( \int_{2}^{3} \frac{7 x^{2}}{\left(x^{3} - 8\right)^{2}}\,dx \), or show that it diverges.

worked_solution.text: The integral is improper because the integrand is unbounded as x approaches 2 from the right, so write it as \( \lim_{R\to 2^{+}} \int_{R}^{3} \frac{7 x^{2}}{\left(x^{3} - 8\right)^{2}}\,dx \).
Substitute \( u = x^{3} - 8,\ du = 3 x^{2}\,dx \). The limits become \( u = R^{3} - 8 \text{ to } u = 19 \), and an antiderivative in u is \( - \frac{7}{3 u} \).
Evaluate the limit: \( \lim_{R\to 2^{+}} \left( - \frac{7}{57} + \frac{7}{3 \left(R^{3} - 8\right)} \right) = \infty \). The limit is infinite, so the integral diverges.

options.label: The integral converges to \( - \frac{7}{57} \).
options.derivation: the term at the singular endpoint, 1 over u at u = 0, treated as 0

options.label: The integral converges to \( \infty - \frac{7}{57} \).
options.derivation: the singular endpoint substituted directly, 1 over 0 written as infinity, and the difference written as a value

options.label: The integral converges to \( - \frac{7}{19} \).
options.derivation: the factor 1/3 from du dropped, then a finite value reported as in the first error
